set_text.text: What is the breakeven on a price change?

The breakeven on a price change is how much volume you can lose after a raise before profit drops below today's. After a cut, it is how much volume you must add. It compares contribution per case before and after the move.
The breakeven treats the $22.00 product cost as your only cost per case. Lose cases at an account and the truck still stops there, so each remaining case costs more to deliver.
Lost volume can hide in the mix
An account can answer a raise by switching to a cheaper line you also carry. Its total cases hold steady, so the loss hides unless you check the item itself.
An account on a fixed price term or a cost-plus contract cannot take a 5% list move mid-term. Run the breakeven on the volume you can actually reprice.
Who uses a price change calculator
It is built for independent food distributors deciding whether to move a price. Anyone who has to defend a raise or sign off on a cut should know the volume line first.
